title: Retrieval Refusal Probe Set
description: Phase IA WS3 (D4.1) — canonical contract for a per-course refusal-probe set, archived at LibV2/courses/<slug>/retrieval_eval/refusal_probes.json. A refusal-probe set is a curated list of UNANSWERABLE questions for one course — questions a correct grounded-answer pipeline must REFUSE (status refused_*), not hallucinate. Probes are the negative half of the refusal-calibration corpus (the gold set supplies the answerable positives); the calibration step sweeps the answerable-vs-unanswerable retrieval-score distributions and proposes thresholds, honestly falling back to v0-uncalibrated permissive defaults when the distributions overlap. Each probe is VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: the required dry_run block records an actual read-only retrieval pass against the live course corpus (top score, result count, and a human confirmation that the top retrieved passage does NOT answer the question) so the 'unanswerable' claim is evidence-backed and re-auditable. This is a SEPARATE schema from gold_set.schema.json (which is WS1-frozen and pinned by WS2 consumers); it is NOT a gold-set bump. Validated by lib/tests/test_refusal_policy.py + schemas/tests/test_refusal_probes_schema.py.

schema_version.description: Refusal-probe schema version. Const-pinned in v1; a future shape change bumps this and ships a new schema file rather than mutating v1 in place.

course_slug.description: LibV2 course slug these probes are authored for (e.g. 'intro-bio-101'). Matches the directory under LibV2/courses/.

authored_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp recording when the probe set was authored.

engine.description: Optional: the retrieval engine the dry-run evidence was recorded against. 'lexical' is the only engine available pre-WS2-E3; semantic dry-runs are re-recorded once the index is built. Defaults to lexical when omitted.

_operator_note.description: Optional free-text note to the operator (e.g. scale-up / re-verify-after-rechunk hand-off). Permitted so seed files can carry out-of-executor-scope flags inline.

probes.description: The unanswerable probe questions. Each carries its category, a human rationale for why the corpus cannot answer it, and a verified retrieval dry-run.

probe_id.description: Refusal-probe id. Pattern rp-<course_slug>-NNNN (4-digit zero-padded ordinal). Mirrors the gold-set gq- convention. Loader enforces uniqueness within the set.

question_text.description: The unanswerable question a correct pipeline must refuse. Min 10 chars.

category.description: Probe taxonomy (D4.1). off_topic: a question from a wholly different discipline the corpus does not touch. adjacent_domain: a plausible neighbour topic the corpus demonstrably lacks (the hardest negatives — they share vocabulary, so the dry-run is the proof of absence). out_of_scope_detail: a question about the course's own topic at a depth/specificity the corpus does not cover (e.g. version-history minutiae).

why_unanswerable.description: Human rationale (>= 20 chars) for why this corpus cannot answer the probe — the design intent behind the negative. Distinct from the dry_run evidence, which is the empirical confirmation.

derived_from_gold_question_id.description: Optional: gold-question id this probe is the out-of-scope twin of (out_of_scope_detail probes often perturb a real gold question to a depth the corpus lacks). Audit aid, not scored.

dry_run.description: Verified-not-assumed evidence: an actual read-only retrieval pass against the live course corpus at authoring time. The 'unanswerable' claim stands on top_passage_answers=false (a human confirmed the top retrieved passage does not answer the question) PLUS the recorded score signal — never on score alone (lexical BM25 scores are corpus-dependent and stopword overlap inflates off-topic scores, so a low score is supporting, not sufficient, evidence).

verified.description: Must be true: a seed probe with verified=false is not a verified-unanswerable probe and is rejected. The dry-run was actually run.

engine.description: Retrieval engine the dry-run used. lexical pre-WS2-E3.

limit.description: top-k limit the dry-run retrieval used.

n_results.description: Number of passages retrieved (0 when the corpus shares no tokens with the probe — the cleanest unanswerable signal).

top_score.description: Score of the rank-1 retrieved passage (0.0 when n_results==0). Recorded for the calibration distribution; not a pass/fail by itself.

top_passage_answers.description: Must be false: a human confirmed the top retrieved passage does NOT answer the probe. If a passage actually answers it, the probe is mis-labelled (the question IS answerable) and must be removed or re-categorised — verified=true with top_passage_answers=true is a contradiction the schema forbids.

top_chunk_id.description: Optional: chunk id of the rank-1 passage (empty/absent when n_results==0). Lets an auditor re-read exactly the passage the verifier judged non-answering.

metadata_scoring.description: Optional: whether the dry-run included the lexical metadata boosts (concept-graph / LO). Recorded because boosts inflate scores; the calibration run pins the scoring mode it used.

verified_at.description: Optional: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the dry-run.

authoring.description: Provenance of this probe. Seed probes are method:manual, status:seed, reviewed_by:PENDING_REVIEW until operator review backfills the reviewer.

method.description: How the probe was authored. manual: hand-authored by the executor; the unanswerability is confirmed by the recorded dry-run.

author.description: @handle or tool id of the author.

reviewed_by.description: @handle of the reviewer, or PENDING_REVIEW for un-reviewed seed probes.

status.description: Authoring lifecycle. seed: deterministic executor-authored starter (verified by dry-run); draft: in-progress; reviewed: operator-approved.
